claims.text: The starting coating consists of an FCC matrix containing BCC precipitates with coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Stabilized, coherent FCC/BCC phase boundaries enhance creep resistance.
Coherent FCC/BCC boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Coherent FCC/BCC boundaries mediate dislocation transfer between phases.
Stabilized phase boundaries dissipate local stresses.
Stabilized interfaces hinder the initiation and propagation of damaging shear bands.
Stabilized interfaces promote controlled dislocation glide across the FCC and BCC phases.
Controlled cross-phase dislocation glide redistributes local strain.
Redistribution of local strain reduces the overall creep strain rate.
A minor element segregating at an interface can weaken the chemical or structural stability of FCC/BCC boundaries.
Coatings with intentionally stabilized boundaries will have a lower creep strain rate than coatings with destabilized boundaries.
Coatings with intentionally stabilized boundaries will exhibit less localized shear deformation and less shear-band development.
The proposed behavior applies at elevated temperature under sustained stresses sufficient to induce progressive plastic deformation but below catastrophic failure.
The mechanism applies only while the coating remains microstructurally stable and no unrelated phase transformation occurs.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction and shear-band suppression may depend on composition and test temperature.

contradictions.description: The intervention calls the optimized, stabilized formulation the baseline, while the baseline field describes a standard formulation with normally stable boundaries and the predicted outcome then compares the optimized sample with the baseline. This makes it unclear whether optimized and baseline are the same group or distinct controls.
